content.text:
I could not retrieve the 2-year yield from the allow-listed sites, so the 2-year half of `cond.curve_rise` has no same-source data yet. The 20-year series is covered only through 15 October 2026. Two threshold values are still missing. Each is listed below.

**Premise 1: Is a cut currently being priced?**
The Fed moved the other way in September.

citations.cited_text: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12 – 0 vote: The Committee decided to raise the target range for t...
citations.title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement

content.text: The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent
. Minutes say

citations.cited_text: With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for th...
citations.title: FOMC Minutes, September 15-16, 2026

content.text: most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end.
A Governor's October speech adds that

citations.cited_text: Sixteen of the 18 participants who submitted dots anticipated at least one more hike during the two remaining meetings this year.
citations.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook - Federal Reserve Board

content.text: Sixteen of the 18 participants who submitted dots anticipated at least one more hike during the two remaining meetings this year.
The next meeting is

citations.cited_text: It was agreed that the next meeting of the Committee would be held on Tuesday–Wednesday, October 27–28, 2026.
citations.title: FOMC Minutes, September 15-16, 2026

content.text: Tuesday–Wednesday, October 27–28, 2026.

**Premise 2: Does a cut pass through to long yields?**
- Baseline from a past easing episode: in May 2025,

citations.cited_text: The Treasury yield curve steepened materially, as short-term Treasury yields declined about 20 basis points over the intermeeting period while longer-...
citations.title: FOMC Minutes, May 6-7, 2025

content.text: short-term Treasury yields declined about 20 basis points over the intermeeting period while longer-term yields increased on net.
The same minutes say

citations.cited_text: The increase in longer-term yields appeared to be partly attributable to higher term premiums.
citations.title: FOMC Minutes, May 6-7, 2025

content.text: The increase in longer-term yields appeared to be partly attributable to higher term premiums.
- Term premium in 2026: the September minutes say

citations.cited_text: Market commentary pointed to geopolitical developments, uncertainty related to the U.S. Treasury's announcement and implementation of the buyback prog...
citations.title: FOMC Minutes, September 15-16, 2026

content.text: Market commentary pointed to geopolitical developments, uncertainty related to the U.S. Treasury's announcement and implementation of the buyback program, and competition for capital from heavy private debt issuance to finance the development of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure as also contributing to higher term premiums and Treasury yields.
- Anchoring (the premise of `cond.curve_rise`): Vice Chair Jefferson said

citations.cited_text: Most measures of longer-term inflation expectations, however, have remained stable at levels consistent with 2 percent inflation.
citations.title: Speech by Vice Chair Jefferson on the U.S. economy and monetary policy - Federal Reserve Board

content.text: Most measures of longer-term inflation expectations, however, have remained stable at levels consistent with 2 percent inflation.
He also warned that

citations.cited_text: But if actual inflation remains above our target, then households and businesses may eventually stop believing that we will return inflation to 2 perc...
citations.title: Speech by Vice Chair Jefferson on the U.S. economy and monetary policy - Federal Reserve Board

content.text: if actual inflation remains above our target, then households and businesses may eventually stop believing that we will return inflation to 2 percent.

**Series data (20-year Treasury constant maturity)**
The Fed's H.15 release reports the 20-year constant maturity, and the Fed states that

. The H.15 table shows the 20-year nominal yield at

content.text: 5.65 on October 9, 5.60 on October 13, 5.57 on October 14, and 5.48 on October 15, 2026

. The 2026-10-27 reference level is not available yet. The FOMC decision is due on the second day of that meeting (28 October), so the 27 October close comes before the announcement. That timing is a fact about the calendar, not a judgment about the rule.

**Thresholds still needed from the user**
- `cond.curve_rise`: the size of the 20-year rise (vs. 2026-10-27 close) that counts as a term-premium shock. The 2-year comparison also needs a source.
- `cond.yield_fall`: the size of the 20-year decline (vs. 2026-10-27 close) that counts as pass-through.

**What I found**
- The Fed raised rates in September 2026 to 3¾–4%, which is the opposite of the cut in the thesis (

citations.cited_text: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12 – 0 vote: The Committee decided to raise the target range for t...

).
- Officials' projections as of October point to further hikes, not cuts (

citations.title: Speech by Governor Waller on the economic outlook - Federal Reserve Board

content.text: The projections submitted at the September meeting showed that a large majority of FOMC participants believe it will be appropriate to raise rates at least once more this year.

).
- The 20-year yield fell from 5.65 to 5.48 between 9 and 15 October (
